---
title: Templates
description: Scaffold a working Barkpark app with create-barkpark-app.
---

`create-barkpark-app` writes a complete project — a Next.js front end, the schemas,
sample content, and a `docker-compose.yml` that brings up the Phoenix API and
Postgres. It is the shortest route from nothing to a site you can edit in Studio.

```bash
npm create barkpark-app my-site
# pnpm create barkpark-app my-site  ·  pnpm dlx cba my-site
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-t, --template <name>` | `website-starter` or `blog-starter`. |
| `--hosted-demo` | Point at the public read-only dataset at `https://barkpark.dev` instead of running Docker. |
| `-y, --yes` | Accept every default. |
| `--skip-install` | Do not run the package install. |
| `--skip-git` | Do not `git init`. |

## The two templates

**`blog-starter`** — a blog. Schemas: `post`, `author`, `tag`. A paginated home
feed, author pages, tag archives, draft-mode preview, per-page metadata with
OpenGraph, `sitemap.ts` and `robots.ts`, and branded `not-found` / `error` /
`loading` states. The seed script writes 2 authors, 3 tags, and 7 posts, one of
them left as a draft so preview has something to show.

**`website-starter`** — a marketing site. Schemas: `page`, `post`, `author`.

Both are Next.js 15 App Router on React 19 and TypeScript, wired with
`@barkpark/nextjs` for server fetching and draft mode, `@barkpark/react`'s
`PortableDoc` for rich text, and Tailwind CSS.

## After the scaffold

```bash
cd my-site
cp .env.example .env.local
docker compose up -d       # Phoenix API on :4000, Postgres on :5432
npm run seed               # sample content
npm run barkpark generate  # TypeScript types from the schemas
npm run dev                # Next.js on :3000
```

The app is on `http://localhost:3000` and Studio on
`http://localhost:4000/studio`. Edit a post in Studio and the change reaches the
site through the webhook handler the template already ships.

One step is easy to miss: `.env.example` ships the placeholder token
`changeme-barkpark-dev-token`. Replace it in `.env.local` with
`barkpark-dev-token`, the value the API seeds on first boot, or every
authenticated call fails.

That dev token carries read, write, and admin scope and must not survive into
production. The templates enforce it — with `NODE_ENV=production` and no
`BARKPARK_SERVER_TOKEN` set, `lib/barkpark.ts` throws at startup instead of
quietly falling back to the dev token.
